[2023 summer phd probability — problem 2]

Part I, Exercise 2. Let $X$ be a discrete random variable valued in $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ with $P(X = j) > 0$ for all $j$.
For any integer $k \in \{1, \dots, n-1\}$ and events $E = \{X \ge k\}$, $F = \{X \ge k+1\}$, prove $\mathbb{E}[X \mid E] \le \mathbb{E}[X \mid F]$.

response.text:
Let

\[
E=\{X\ge k\}, \qquad F=\{X\ge k+1\}.
\]

Since \(P(X=j)>0\) for every \(j\in\{1,\dots,n\}\), both \(E\) and \(F\) have positive probability, so the conditional expectations are well-defined.

Observe that

\[
E=\{X=k\}\cup F,
\]

and this union is disjoint. Therefore, conditioning on \(E\), the random variable \(X\) is either equal to \(k\), or else lies in \(F\). Hence

\[
\mathbb{E}[X\mid E]
=
\mathbb{E}[X\mid X=k]P(X=k\mid E)
+
\mathbb{E}[X\mid F]P(F\mid E).
\]

Since \(\mathbb{E}[X\mid X=k]=k\), this becomes

\[
\mathbb{E}[X\mid E]
=
k\,P(X=k\mid E)+\mathbb{E}[X\mid F]P(F\mid E).
\]

Also,

\[
P(X=k\mid E)+P(F\mid E)=1.
\]

Now on the event \(F=\{X\ge k+1\}\), we have \(X\ge k+1\), so

\[
\mathbb{E}[X\mid F]\ge k+1>k.
\]

Thus \(k\le \mathbb{E}[X\mid F]\). Therefore,

\[
\mathbb{E}[X\mid E]
=
k\,P(X=k\mid E)+\mathbb{E}[X\mid F]P(F\mid E)
\le
\mathbb{E}[X\mid F]P(X=k\mid E)+\mathbb{E}[X\mid F]P(F\mid E).
\]

Factoring the right-hand side gives

\[
\mathbb{E}[X\mid E]
\le
\mathbb{E}[X\mid F]\bigl(P(X=k\mid E)+P(F\mid E)\bigr)
=
\mathbb{E}[X\mid F].
\]

Hence,

\[
\boxed{\mathbb{E}[X\mid X\ge k]\le \mathbb{E}[X\mid X\ge k+1].}
\]

In fact, because \(P(X=k)>0\) and \(P(F)>0\), the inequality is strict.
